chapter: La Cigalle and settling in Paris
title: Jacques Butler's band changes at the Cigalle
summary: Waters worked with Butler for a couple of years until the band was fired. Butler returned later and other bands came in, including a bebop group and the Guadeloupean trombonist Al Levrat.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: OK, we've also changed and leaped into the '80's, let's go back to '55. You knew
Jacques Butler from the States - how did you know Jacques Butler, how did he find you to -
Well, I saw Jacques Butler saying - you know who he just worked with, Horace Henderson -
Yeah, years ago, is that right?
Yes, I - and a lot of other people, yeah.
Yeah, he was here January 26th of '81.
He's here, he's here in New York.

Well, see, I worked with Jacques Butler, quite a while I worked down there with Jacques. Well, I worked with Jacques several times, different times. Because I worked with Jacques a couple of years, then the band changed hands and then for some reason they fired the band.
So this is La Cigalle, you got in and play Fifty -
So they fired the Jacques Butler band and then brought you back again.
Yeah. They fired Jacques - well, Jacques's back again.
Uh huh, but not you 'cause you weren't with -

I don't know if they fired him or Jacques left, I think it was some kind of trouble. Anyway Jacques left the place, I'll make it that way. He left the place, then he got another band - kinda bebop band, little Martinique saxophone player, tried to copy Charlie Parker and so forth. Then Al Levy [Levitt?] the trombone player went in there and he was tryin' to play some of the more modern things that he heard in New York like Benny Golson, all that type, see. And then they wasn't used to that, he was, they were used to entertaining and Jacques used to sing a little bit, you know? And I would sing my little comic song like I do now and make little arrangements, you know, see, and we had little things going.
